q.t: What is the beat?
o: The steady pulse you clap along to
The loudest note in a song
The highest note in a song
The last note of a song
q.e: The beat is the steady pulse — clap, clap, clap — that note lengths are measured against.

q.t: How many beats does a whole note last?
q.e: Whole = 4 beats.

q.t: How many beats does a half note last?
q.e: Half of a whole note: 4 ÷ 2 = 2 beats.

q.t: How many beats does a quarter note last?
q.e: A quarter of a whole note: 4 ÷ 4 = 1 beat.

q.t: How long is an eighth note?
q.e: Half of a quarter note: ½ beat. Two eighths fill one beat.

q.t: How do you count eighth notes out loud?
q.e: The '&' falls exactly halfway between two beats.

q.t: What is a rest?
q.e: A rest is silence that you still count, so the next note comes in on time.

q.t: What does a tie do?
o: Joins two notes into one longer note
q.e: Play once, then hold for the length of both notes.

q.t: In strumming, ↓ means…
q.e: ↓ = down-strum, ↑ = up-strum.

q.t: Down-strums usually fall on…
q.e: The hand goes down on the beat and up on the '&', like a pendulum.

q.t: Which note is drawn as a filled oval with a stem and one flag?
q.e: One flag (or one beam) = eighth note.

q.t: Which note is drawn as a hollow oval with a stem?
q.e: Hollow + stem = half note. Hollow with no stem = whole note.

q.t: How many quarter notes make one whole note?
q.e: 4 × 1 beat = 4 beats.

q.t: How many eighth notes make one half note?
q.e: A half note is 2 beats; each eighth is ½ beat: 2 ÷ ½ = 4.

q.t: How many beats does a dotted half note last?
q.e: A dot adds half the note's length: 2 + 1 = 3.

q.t: How do you count sixteenth notes?
q.e: Four sixteenths in each beat: 1 e & a.

q.t: A half note + a quarter + a quarter = how many beats?
Why should you count out loud while playing?
q.e: In your head the beat drifts — faster on easy bits, slower on hard bits. Counting out loud holds it steady.

q.t: Why do we count rests instead of skipping them?
o: So the next note comes in on time
So you can tune during them
q.e: Silence is part of the rhythm. Skip the count and the next note comes too early.

q.t: Why are notes called 'half', 'quarter' and 'eighth'?
o: They are fractions of a whole note
They are played by fewer fingers
q.e: A quarter note is ¼ of a whole note; an eighth is ⅛ of it.

q.t: How many beats does a dotted quarter note last?
q.e: 1 + half of 1 = 1½.

q.t: A half note tied to a quarter note lasts…
q.e: A tie adds the two: 2 + 1 = 3.

q.t: Three eighth notes last how many beats?
How many sixteenth notes make one quarter note?
q.e: Each sixteenth is ¼ beat: 1 ÷ ¼ = 4.

q.t: Four eighth notes + one half note = how many beats?
In Jingle Bells, 'bells' is a half note starting on beat 3. Until which count does it ring?
o: Through beat 1 of the next bar
q.e: A half note lasts 2 beats: 3 and 4.

q.t: A dot adds…
o: half the length of that note
q.e: A dot after a half note adds 1; a dot after a quarter adds ½. It depends on the note.

q.t: Strum pattern ↓ ↓↑ ↓ ↓↑ — on which counts are the up-strums?
Why does your strumming hand keep moving even on strums you skip?
o: So every strum lands on time
q.e: A hand that never stops is like a clock — you just choose when it touches the strings.

q.t: On an electric guitar, what must you do during a rest?
q.e: A rest is silence, so mute the strings with either hand.

q.t: How many sixteenth notes fit in a whole note?
q.e: 4 beats × 4 sixteenths per beat = 16.

q.t: A dotted half note + a quarter note = how many beats?
A dotted quarter + an eighth = how many beats?
Which group adds up to exactly 4 beats?
q.e: 3 + 1 = 4. The others: 5, 5, 3.

q.t: Which group adds up to exactly 3 beats?
q.e: 2 + ½ + ½ = 3. The others: 4, 4, 3½.

q.t: How many beats does a dotted eighth note last?
q.e: ½ + half of ½ (= ¼) = ¾ beat.

q.t: Two half notes tied together last…
q.e: 2 + 2 = 4 — played once and held.

q.t: Which rest equals a half note in length?
q.e: Every note length has a matching rest of the same length.

q.t: In 1 e & a, where does the 'a' fall?
o: Three-quarters of the way through the beat
q.e: 1 = start, e = ¼, & = ½, a = ¾ of the way through the beat.

q.t: Why do we need dots and ties at all?
o: Plain notes only halve, so 3 or 1½ beats need them
To show which string to play
To mark the end of a song
q.e: Plain notes are 4, 2, 1, ½ … To get lengths in between, add a dot or join two notes with a tie.
